title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned The Pass. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Pass
options.lineage: a restaurant expo pass: steel ticket rail, two-ink kitchen printers, heat lamps
options.thesis: Your projects hang on the pass as live order tickets, the systems you actually build.
options.viewport: Your name and one line above a steel rail; four project tickets hang from it, Signal404 stamped live in printer red.
options.risk: Becomes a restaurant costume if the copy makes kitchen puns; the world stays in the material, the words stay plain.

raised.raise: Three inks only: thermal black, printer red and paper on steel, no other hue anywhere.
Tickets are billed by rank: Vela prints at twice the length of the rest.
Light and dark are the two services: daylight prep on bright steel, night service under heat lamps.
The rail sits off-centre and tickets hang at their own torn lengths; asymmetry is the rule.

options.label: Drawing Set
options.lineage: engineering drawing sheets with a title block and revision table
options.thesis: Every project is a sheet in your drawing set, with the resume as the title block.
options.viewport: A drawing sheet: your name in the title block bottom-right, Vela's system drawn as the main view.
options.risk: Blueprints are a familiar developer-portfolio move; this one reads safe.

options.label: Select Rail
options.lineage: a film cutting bench: perforated work print, tape flags, trims on pins
options.thesis: Your work strung as frames on one perforated rail, the one you are reading flagged.
options.viewport: A frame strip across the screen, each project a frame, the open one flagged in orange.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads well, but film editing is not your world, so recruiters and clients identify less.
options.risk: Orange on black is close to a common dark-portfolio look.

options.label: Emission Lines
options.lineage: a spectrogram plate: charcoal continuum crossed by hairline emission lines
options.thesis: Your career as a calibrated plate, every project a line on one off-centre rail.
options.viewport: A spectrum band with each project as a bright line; the open one blooms into a plate.
options.case: Matches the technical tone engineers like; clients read lines instead of projects, so it is less clear.
options.risk: Abstract: the work hides behind the instrument.

options.label: Rebel Menu
options.lineage: game menu collage in red, black and white
options.thesis: Every section a torn cutout slammed onto a scarlet field.
options.viewport: A scarlet splash with sheared italic headings.
options.case: Loses both axes: loud for hiring, and it says nothing about your work.
options.kept: Total palette commitment: three inks only.

options.label: Combo Sheet
options.thesis: Two titles shouting over a billing block.
options.viewport: A shouting poster with agate billing.
options.case: Loses both axes: novelty over clarity.
options.kept: Billing by rank: size says what matters most.

options.label: Night City
options.thesis: A skyline whose lights are your projects.
options.viewport: A rainy skyline at blue hour.
options.case: Loses both axes: atmosphere without proof.
options.kept: Light and dark as two times of day, each with its own logic.

options.label: Raku Smoke
options.lineage: raku firing: soot clay, crackled glaze
options.thesis: Projects fired and cooled into cracked vessels.
options.viewport: A smoking vessel and brush marks.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to software or hiring.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: name and role, a grid of project cards, an experience timeline.
canonCard.viewport: Name, role and buttons up top, three project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other developer portfolio by design.
